[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 — the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.

WHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.

THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.
- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` — takes the MOST important open representability item.
- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts — propose to the human instead).

STANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.

WHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:
- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.
- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.
- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P → P`.
- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.

COMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.

    76	`baseOpenRankOneDivisor_awayMul_compat`. The big-site consumer scaffold reduces
    77	`PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen` to one canonical evaluation-divisor classifier and per-test pullback
    78	squares: `picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_evaluationDivisorPullbackFamilies`.
    79	
    80	The glued divisor now descends: `existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation` consumes
    81	the finite-glue output and returns the unique Abel-correct `DivFamZarAff` over the original
    82	affine base, conditional only on the named `RankOneDivisorUniqueness` interface (the
    83	tensor-square cocycle is manufactured from uniqueness, the descended class is pinned by étale
    84	separatedness); `canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation` names that divisor. Toward discharging
    85	the uniqueness interface, `exists_notMem_cechPicMap_eq_of_relPicMk_eq` localizes
    86	`relPicMk`-equality to on-the-nose `picClass` equality near every prime (base Picard classes
    87	die Zariski-locally). The public locus is fibrewise split:
    88	`mem_picRankOneOpen_iff_isSplitWitness` at field bases, and
    89	`isSplitWitness_testPoint_of_mem` at every point of an arbitrary test.
    90	
    91	Fibre nonvanishing toward that discharge is landed:
    92	`sectionsMapTop_ne_zero_of_divEq_certified` and its tensor-form consumer say a datum section
    93	cutting a certified divisor is nonzero on every residue-field fibre — the exact input shape of
    94	the rank-one unit-extraction engine.
    95	
    96	Datum-section extraction is landed, Noetherian-free:
    97	`exists_gluedSection_sectionLocalEquations_divEq` cuts any `LocalEquations` divisor whose
    98	Picard class matches the datum's Čech class from a germ-regular global section of the glued
    99	sheaf, up to `DivEq` on every subordinated pointed cover — the α-corrected gluing through the
   100	glued sheaf's own sheaf property; and `sectionLocalEquations_smul_divEq` records that global
   101	unit rescalings of the section do not move the cut divisor.
   102	
   103	The uniqueness interface is now DISCHARGED: `divFamZarAff_eq_of_picClass_eq_cechPicClass`
   104	proves at most one certified divisor family per rank-one datum class (extraction + fibre
   105	nonvanishing + the unit-extraction engine), and `rankOneDivisorUniqueness` assembles it with
   106	the base-discrepancy localization, away-span separatedness, and faithfully-flat descent into
   107	an unconditional proof of `RankOneDivisorUniqueness`. The canonical rank-one divisor and its
   108	Abel/uniqueness accessors are re-exported without the interface hypothesis
   109	(`canonicalRankOneDivisor`).
   110	
   111	The Abel inverse law is also discharged: `divFamZarAff_eq_of_rankOne` upgrades the affine
   112	uniqueness to arbitrary tests through the vehicle's affine-open separatedness, so the
   113	restricted Abel map is componentwise injective on the big site
   114	(`rankOneAbelSigma_app_injective`) and every evaluation-divisor classifier is automatically a
   115	two-sided inverse (`abelInverse_of_uniqueness`); `rankOneAbelIso` packages the isomorphism,
   116	gated only on an inhabitant of `PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData`.
   117	
   118	The noetherian-free canonical divisor theorem is now integrated at family level:
   119	`canonicalRankOneSection` is natural on every test scheme, its representer transport is
   120	`canonicalRankOneRepresenterTrans`, and `canonicalRankOneEvaluationDivisorData` is a genuine
   121	inhabitant of the evaluator contract.  The finite-stage degree, admissibility, glued-divisor,
   122	carrier transport, arbitrary-affine canonical divisor, and family integration milestones are
   123	independently kernel-checked.  Consequently `canonicalRankOneAbelIso` is a root-reachable
   124	two-sided inverse to the restricted Abel map on the big site.
   125	
   126	The geometric open-locus producer is now unconditional.  `picRankOneSplitLocus` is open on an
   127	arbitrary test, pointwise splitting constructs the native presentation of the same pulled-back
   128	class, and `picRankOneOpen_fibrePresented` identifies this open with the pullback of the public
   129	rank-one locus along an arbitrary Yoneda family.  Thus `picRankOneOpen_isOpen`, specialized to
   130	`divRepAffP1Map C`, supplies the actual `DivRankOneOpenData` consumed by the canonical Abel chart.
   131	
   132	The generic finite-Galois quotient engine is also complete through non-affine stable-chart
   133	gluing.  `galoisQuotientWitnessOfInvariantProjection` supplies the effective universal
   134	property, while `StableAffineOpen.isGaloisQuotient_glued` and
   135	`StableAffineOpen.hasGaloisQuotient_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` construct the quotient under the
   136	honest orbit-in-affine-open condition.  `GaloisQuotientWitness.overHomEquiv` and
   137	`StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv` now identify arbitrary maps into those quotients
   138	with equivariant maps after base change, naturally under precomposition.  The Picard-zero
   139	comparison is now matched on both sides: `pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver`
   140	identifies deck-invariant classes with equivariant maps for the semilinear action on a chosen
   141	finite-level representer, and its `_precomp` theorem supplies the needed naturality.  Thus
   142	`pic0RepresentableBy_finiteGaloisDescent` immediately turns a finite-Galois Picard-zero
   143	representer into a descended `RepresentableBy` certificate, under the explicit
   144	`OrbitsInAffineOpen` hypothesis.  This producer is deliberately conditional: it does not
   145	manufacture either the finite-stage representer or the orbit-in-affine-open input.
   146	
   147	The separably closed endpoint is now complete.  The exact translator returned by
   148	`exists_sepClosedTranslated_mem_picRankOneOpen` indexes a translated canonical Abel chart;
   149	these charts are open immersions and cover every residue-field point.  Consequently
   150	`pic0_sepClosed_representableBy` is unconditional and represents the same pinned
   151	`pic0TypeFunctor` over every separably closed base field.  The widened admissible Abel chart
   152	is etale-locally surjective onto this exact carrier, so its quasi-compact source proves
   153	`quasiCompact_pic0SepClosedRepresenter`; `picRepDatumSepClosed` and
   154	`jacobianDataSepClosed` package that same carrier and the same representation without
   155	changing either component.  The same carrier is also finitely presented and quasi-separated,
   156	the exact geometric hypotheses needed by a future finite-subextension object-spread theorem.
   157	
   158	The finite-stage algebraic substrate is now rooted too.  Finitely presented algebras, tensor
   159	coefficients and equalities, etale algebras and covers, Cech and relative-Picard classes, and a
   160	representative PicEt cover all descend to finite subextensions.  A basic-open cocycle datum over
   161	a tensor coefficient ring descends to one finite tensor stage.  The exact separably closed
   162	representer has a chosen finite affine atlas with finitely presented chart rings and finite
   163	affine presentations of pairwise overlaps.  Finally,
   164	`pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit_of_representableBy` proves the filtered-colimit statement once
   165	an arbitrary-field locally finitely presented representer has actually been produced.
   166	
   167	These inputs do not yet constitute object descent.  Still missing, and NOT replaced here by
   168	axioms or local hypotheses: simultaneous finite-stage models for the atlas restriction maps;
   169	chosen overlap transition isomorphisms, triple-overlap cocycles, and a glued-scheme base-change
   170	comparison; descent of the universal Picard natural equivalence; the orbit-in-affine-open input
   171	for the finite-level Picard quotient; and the arbitrary-base-field `pic0_representableBy` and
   172	`JacobianData` endpoints.

30:/-! ## The two slice presentations of a deck transformation -/
31:
32:/-- The deck transformation of a base-changed test, packaged as a morphism in
33:the slice over `Spec L`. -/
34:noncomputable def pic0GalTwistMor
35:    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
36:    (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T) ⟶
37:      baseTest (k' := L) T :=
38:  Over.homMk (pullbackGalMap K L T.hom gamma)
39:    (pullbackGalMap_snd K L T.hom gamma)
40:
41:@[simp]
42:theorem pic0GalTwistMor_left
43:    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
44:    (pic0GalTwistMor T gamma).left = pullbackGalMap K L T.hom gamma :=
45:  rfl
46:
47:/-- Base change of a morphism of `K`-tests, regarded as a morphism of their
48:base changes over `Spec L`. -/
49:noncomputable def pic0GaloisBaseChangeMor
50:    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T) :
51:    baseTest (k' := L) T' ⟶ baseTest (k' := L) T :=
52:  Over.homMk (pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w)
53:    (pullbackBaseChange_snd K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w)
54:
55:theorem pic0GaloisBaseTestMap_eq_restrict_map
56:    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T) :
57:    pic0GaloisBaseTestMap (L := L) a =
58:      (pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := K) (L := L)).map
59:        (pic0GaloisBaseChangeMor (L := L) a) :=
60:  rfl
61:
62:/-- The inverse comparison from a twisted `L`-test to the original test is the
63:identity on underlying schemes. -/

65:    (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (D : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
66:    ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).inv.app D).left = 𝟙 D.left := by
67:  have h := congrArg Over.Hom.left
68:    ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom_inv_id_app D)
69:  rw [Over.comp_left, pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_hom_app_left] at h
70:  have hfixed : @Eq (D.left ⟶ D.left)

9:/-!
10:# The quotient-side bridge for finite Galois descent of Picard zero
11:
12:A specified finite Galois quotient represents equivariant maps after base
13:change.  This file records that statement in the over-category.  It is the
14:scheme-theoretic half of descending a representative of `pic0TypeFunctor`.
15:-/
16:
17:set_option autoImplicit false
18:
19:universe u
20:
21:open CategoryTheory Limits
22:open AlgebraicGeometry
23:
24:namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

26:/-- An equivariant map from the finite-Galois base change of an object over
27:`Spec K` to a semilinearly acted `L`-scheme. -/
28:structure GaloisEquivariantOver
29:    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
30:    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
31:    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
32:    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) where
33:  hom : pullback T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X
34:  commutes : hom ≫ f =
35:    pullback.snd T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
36:  equivariant : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L T.hom).IsEquivariant rho hom

38:namespace GaloisEquivariantOver
39:
40:variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
41:  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
42:  (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
43:
44:/-- Pull an equivariant map back along a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
45:noncomputable def precomp
46:    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
47:    (h : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T) : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T' where
48:  hom := pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w ≫ h.hom
49:  commutes := by
50:    rw [Category.assoc, h.commutes, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
51:  equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
52:    T.hom T'.hom rho h.equivariant a.left a.w
53:
54:@[ext]
55:theorem ext {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
56:    {h h' : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T} (hh : h.hom = h'.hom) : h = h' := by
57:  cases h
58:  cases h'
59:  cases hh
60:  rfl
61:
62:end GaloisEquivariantOver

   261	noncomputable def pic0GaloisTwistMor (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   262	    (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj J ⟶ J :=
   263	  rep.homEquiv.symm
   264	    ((pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op J)
   265	      (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J)))

   270	      (pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op J)
   271	        (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J)) :=
   272	  Equiv.apply_symm_apply _ _

   274	/-- The twist morphisms obey the field-automorphism group law in the slice. -/
   275	theorem pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   276	    pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma * tau) =
   277	      (pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app J ≫
   278	        (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).map
   279	          (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau) ≫
   280	        pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma := by
   281	  apply rep.homEquiv.injective
   282	  rw [pic0Galois_homEquiv_twistMor, rep.homEquiv_comp,
   283	    rep.homEquiv_comp, pic0Galois_homEquiv_twistMor]
   284	  change _ = (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).map
   285	    ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app J).op
   286	      (((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).op ⋙
   287	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).map
   288	          (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau).op
   289	          ((pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op J)
   290	            (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J))))
   291	  rw [← NatTrans.naturality_apply (pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv
   292	    (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau).op (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J))]

   294	  exact pic0GaloisAction_mul_inv_app C gamma tau J

   305	      ((pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso (k := k) (L := L)).hom.app J)).symm

   309	    (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (1 : L ≃ₐ[k] L)).left = 𝟙 J.left := by
   310	  rw [pic0GaloisTwistMor_one]

   313	/-- On underlying schemes, twist morphisms multiply in the order used by
   314	categorical automorphisms. -/
   315	theorem pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul_left (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   316	    (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma * tau)).left =
   317	      (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau).left ≫
   318	        (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left := by
   319	  have h := congrArg Over.Hom.left
   320	    (pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul C rep gamma tau)
   321	  simp only [Over.comp_left, Over.map_map_left] at h
   322	  let m : J.left ⟶ J.left :=
   323	    ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app J).left
   324	  have hfixed : @Eq (J.left ⟶ J.left)
   325	      ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma * tau)).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)
   326	      ((m ≫ ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)) ≫
   327	        ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)) := h
   328	  have hm : m = 𝟙 J.left := by
   329	    dsimp only [m]
   330	    exact pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso_hom_app_left gamma tau J

   334	/-- The twist morphism covers the corresponding automorphism of `Spec L`.
   335	This is the structure equation of the slice morphism itself. -/
   336	theorem pic0GaloisTwistMor_compat (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   337	    (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left ≫ J.hom =
   338	      J.hom ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[k] L) L gamma).hom :=
   339	  Over.w (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma)

   341	/-- The twist at `gamma`, with the inverse-indexed twist as inverse. -/
   342	noncomputable def pic0GaloisTwistAut (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) : Aut J.left where
   343	  hom := (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left
   344	  inv := (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma⁻¹).left
   345	  hom_inv_id := by
   346	    have hfixed : @Eq (J.left ⟶ J.left)
   347	        ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma⁻¹ * gamma)).left :
   348	          J.left ⟶ J.left)
   349	        (((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left : J.left ⟶ J.left) ≫
   350	          ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma⁻¹).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)) :=
   351	      pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul_left C rep gamma⁻¹ gamma
   352	    exact hfixed.symm.trans (by
   353	      rw [inv_mul_cancel gamma]
   354	      exact pic0GaloisTwistMor_one_left C rep)
   355	  inv_hom_id := by
   356	    have hfixed : @Eq (J.left ⟶ J.left)
   357	        ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma * gamma⁻¹)).left :
   358	          J.left ⟶ J.left)
   359	        (((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma⁻¹).left : J.left ⟶ J.left) ≫
   360	          ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)) :=
   361	      pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul_left C rep gamma gamma⁻¹
   362	    exact hfixed.symm.trans (by
   363	      rw [mul_inv_cancel gamma]
   364	      exact pic0GaloisTwistMor_one_left C rep)
   365	
   366	/-- The canonical twists form an action on the underlying representing scheme.
   367	-/
   368	noncomputable def pic0GaloisTwistAction :
   369	    (L ≃ₐ[k] L) →* Aut J.left :=
   370	  MonoidHom.mk' (pic0GaloisTwistAut C rep) fun gamma tau => by
   371	    apply Aut.ext
   372	    exact pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul_left C rep gamma tau

   374	/-- A representation of Picard zero over `L` canonically supplies the
   375	semilinear action required by finite-Galois quotient descent.  No finiteness,
   376	Galois, affine, or additional curve hypothesis is introduced. -/
   377	noncomputable def pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy :
   378	    SemilinearGalAction k L J.left J.hom where
   379	  act := pic0GaloisTwistAction C rep
   380	  compat gamma := pic0GaloisTwistMor_compat C rep gamma
   381

    52	/-- A Galois-invariant Picard-zero class satisfies the kernel-pair equality

    54	theorem pic0GaloisInvariant_pullback_condition

    95	theorem pic0GaloisInvariant_compatible

    99	    {Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}

   123	/-- The Sigma-extension element attached to an invariant class is compatible
   124	for the singleton field-extension cover. -/
   125	theorem pic0GaloisInvariant_sigma_compatible
   126	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
   127	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
   128	    (x : Pic0GaloisInvariant (L := L) C T)
   129	    {Z : Scheme.{u}}
   130	    (p₁ p₂ : Z ⟶ ((restrictTest K L).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T)).left)
   131	    (hp : p₁ ≫ (coverMap (k' := L) T).left =
   132	      p₂ ≫ (coverMap (k' := L) T).left) :
   133	    (pic0SigmaFunctor C).map p₁.op
   134	        ⟨((restrictTest K L).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T)).hom, x.1⟩ =
   135	      (pic0SigmaFunctor C).map p₂.op
   136	        ⟨((restrictTest K L).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T)).hom, x.1⟩ := by
   137	  let B := (restrictTest K L).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T)
   138	  have hbase : p₁ ≫ B.hom = p₂ ≫ B.hom := by
   139	    rw [← Over.w (coverMap (k' := L) T)]
   140	    simpa only [Category.assoc] using congrArg (fun q => q ≫ T.hom) hp
   141	  let ZK : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := Over.mk (p₁ ≫ B.hom)
   142	  let g₁ : ZK ⟶ B := Over.homMk p₁ rfl
   143	  let g₂ : ZK ⟶ B := Over.homMk p₂ hbase.symm
   144	  have hg : g₁ ≫ coverMap (k' := L) T = g₂ ≫ coverMap (k' := L) T := by
   145	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   146	    exact hp
   147	  have hfib : (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g₁.op x.1 =
   148	      (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g₂.op x.1 :=
   149	    pic0GaloisInvariant_compatible C T x g₁ g₂ hg
   150	  let y := (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g₁.op x.1
   151	  have h₁ : (pic0SigmaFunctor C).map p₁.op ⟨B.hom, x.1⟩ =
   152	      ⟨p₁ ≫ B.hom, y⟩ :=
   153	    (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (F := pic0TypeFunctor C)
   154	      p₁ rfl x.1 y).mpr rfl
   155	  have h₂ : (pic0SigmaFunctor C).map p₂.op ⟨B.hom, x.1⟩ =
   156	      ⟨p₁ ≫ B.hom, y⟩ :=
   157	    (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (F := pic0TypeFunctor C)
   158	      p₂ hbase.symm x.1 y).mpr hfib.symm
   159	  exact h₁.trans h₂.symm

   161	/-- Every invariant class descends uniquely along the finite-Galois field
   162	extension cover.  This is the effective-descent half of the comparison. -/
   163	theorem pic0GaloisInvariant_existsUnique_descend
   164	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
   165	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
   166	    (x : Pic0GaloisInvariant (L := L) C T) :
   167	    ∃! y : (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj (op T),
   168	      (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (coverMap (k' := L) T).op y = x.1 := by
   169	  let B := (restrictTest K L).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T)
   170	  let f := (coverMap (k' := L) T).left
   171	  haveI : Etale f := by
   172	    exact Scheme.etale_pullback_fst_specMap K L T.left T.hom
   173	  haveI : Surjective f := by
   174	    exact Scheme.surjective_pullback_fst_specMap K L T.left T.hom
   175	  haveI : Flat f := inferInstance
   176	  haveI : EffectiveEpi f := inferInstance
   177	  have hmem : Presieve.singleton f ∈ Scheme.precoverage (@Etale) T.left := by
   178	    rw [Scheme.singleton_mem_precoverage_iff]
   179	    exact ⟨f.surjective, inferInstance⟩
   180	  have hsheaf : Presieve.IsSheafFor (pic0SigmaFunctor C)
   181	      (Presieve.singleton f) :=
   182	    (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf_etale C).isSheafFor_of_mem_precoverage hmem
   183	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_singleton] at hsheaf
   184	  obtain ⟨⟨a, z⟩, hz, hzu⟩ := hsheaf ⟨B.hom, x.1⟩
   185	    (fun p₁ p₂ hp => pic0GaloisInvariant_sigma_compatible C T x p₁ p₂ hp)
   186	  have hfirst : f ≫ a = B.hom := congrArg Sigma.fst hz
   187	  have hcover : f ≫ T.hom = B.hom := Over.w (coverMap (k' := L) T)
   188	  have ha : a = T.hom := (cancel_epi f).mp (hfirst.trans hcover.symm)
   189	  subst a
   190	  have hz' : (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (coverMap (k' := L) T).op z = x.1 :=
   191	    (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (F := pic0TypeFunctor C)
   192	      f hcover z x.1).mp hz
   193	  refine ⟨z, hz', ?_⟩
   194	  intro y hy
   195	  have hySigma : (pic0SigmaFunctor C).map f.op ⟨T.hom, y⟩ = ⟨B.hom, x.1⟩ :=
   196	    (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (F := pic0TypeFunctor C)
   197	      f hcover y x.1).mpr hy
   198	  have hpair := hzu ⟨T.hom, y⟩ hySigma
   199	  cases hpair
   200	  rfl
   201	
   202	/-- Restriction to the finite-Galois base change is a bijection onto the
   203	Galois-invariant Picard-zero classes. -/
   204	theorem pic0RestrictToGaloisInvariant_bijective
   205	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
   206	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
   207	    Function.Bijective (pic0RestrictToGaloisInvariant (L := L) C T) := by
   208	  constructor
   209	  · intro a b hab
   210	    have hdesc := pic0GaloisInvariant_existsUnique_descend C T
   211	      (pic0RestrictToGaloisInvariant (L := L) C T a)
   212	    apply hdesc.unique
   213	    · rfl
   214	    · exact (congrArg Subtype.val hab).symm
   215	  · intro x
   216	    obtain ⟨y, hy, _⟩ := pic0GaloisInvariant_existsUnique_descend C T x
   217	    exact ⟨y, Subtype.ext hy⟩
   218	
   219	/-- Picard-zero classes over an arbitrary `K`-test scheme are exactly the
   220	classes on its finite-Galois base change fixed by all deck transformations. -/
   221	noncomputable def pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv
   222	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
   223	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
   224	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj (op T) ≃ Pic0GaloisInvariant (L := L) C T :=
   225	  Equiv.ofBijective (pic0RestrictToGaloisInvariant (L := L) C T)
   226	    (pic0RestrictToGaloisInvariant_bijective C T)
   227	
   228	/-- Base change of a morphism of `K`-tests, regarded in the `K`-slice after
   229	restriction from `L`. -/
   230	noncomputable def pic0GaloisBaseTestMap
   231	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T) :
   232	    (restrictTest K L).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T') ⟶
   233	      (restrictTest K L).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T) :=
   234	  (restrictTest K L).map
   235	    (Over.homMk (pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w)
   236	      (pullbackBaseChange_snd K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w))
   237	
   238	/-- The base-changed test map commutes with the field-extension covers. -/
   239	theorem pic0GaloisBaseTestMap_comp_coverMap
   240	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T) :
   241	    pic0GaloisBaseTestMap (L := L) a ≫ coverMap (k' := L) T =
   242	      coverMap (k' := L) T' ≫ a := by
   243	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   244	  exact pullbackBaseChange_fst K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w
   245	
   246	/-- Base change of test schemes commutes with each deck transformation. -/
   247	theorem twistTest_naturality
   248	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)

    14	representative, and applying naturality of the quotient map.

    26	finite subextension. -/

    28	    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
    29	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    30	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
    31	    (q : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
    32	    ∃ L : DatG0.FinSubext k K, ∃ qL : relPic C (overSpec k L.1),
    33	      relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k L.1 K) qL = q := by
    34	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k K) q
    35	  obtain ⟨L, cL, hcL⟩ := exists_finSubext_cechPic_model C π c

    32	on the base change of an etale cover from a finite subextension.  The representative's descent
    33	class is still defined over the full field `K`. -/
    34	theorem exists_finSubext_baseChanged_cover_representation
    35	    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
    36	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (x : PicEtAff C K) :
    37	    ∃ (L : DatG0.FinSubext k K) (E₀ : Algebra.EtaleCover L.1)

    39	      PicEtAff.mk C (E₀.baseChange K) ξK = x := by
    40	  induction x using PicEtAff.ind with

    43	        DatG0.exists_finSubext_etaleCover_model (k := k) (K := K) E
